chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Al-Nufali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Urinating while standing without a valid excuse is from Al-Jafa' (coarseness/ lack of refinement), and cleansing oneself with the right hand is from Al-Jafa'.
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Al-Jafa' refer to in the context of urination and cleansing in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these acts under 'Al-Jafa' (coarseness), contrasting them with 'Al-Jud' (refinement) to illustrate how mundane physical habits reflect spiritual and social elegance. This narration emphasizes that proper hygiene and posture are not merely ritualistic requirements but indicators of a refined character (*adab*) in Shia ethical tradition. The prohibition of using the right hand for cleansing highlights the distinction between the sacred (used for eating and greeting) and the mundane, reinforcing the holistic nature of bodily purity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-72 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB) , on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
Urinating while standing up without a proper excuse and cleansing oneself with the right hand after defecation are both acts that are harmful to oneself.”
